newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bill yields seen below market at auction.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bill yields seen below market at auction.

text.p: Strong demand from non-residents for long-dated GKO discount Treasury bills and OFZ government bonds will enable the Finance Ministry to place paper on Wednesday at or below market yields, dealers said on Tuesday.
TOMORROW
Finance Ministry sells:
* 7.50 trillion roubles 364-day bills (series 23005)
* 4.00 trillion rbls new 707-day new bond tranche (series 24011)
Finance Ministry repays/pays:
* 6.91 trillion roubles maturing 182-day bills (22055)
* 246.86 billion roubles interest on 2-yr bond (24009)
TODAY
* Average yield fell to 30.5 from 31.7 percent
* Turnover rose to 6.01 trillion from 3.11 trillion roubles
* Series 24011 bonds close at 98.85 percent
* Series 23003 bills close at 76.59 to yield 31.78 percent
* Central bank raised 50.8 billion roubles by selling 23003 bills and 24011 bonds

Dealers forecast the average yield of the new one-year bills, which mature on April 22, 1998, would be in a 31.34-33.37 percent range. The series 23003 one-year bills maturing April 8 next year closed with a yield of 31.78 percent.
They forecast the average price of the new tranche of 24011 bonds, maturing March 31, 1999, in a 98.56-99.87 percent range. The earlier tranche closed at 98.85 percent.
"I think there will be a strong element of non-resident demand at the auction, because the market already saw a rise in prices today," said Robert Devane, head of fixed income at Troika Dialog.
"Strong demand will allow the Finance Ministry to carry out the auction in comfort and the one-year paper will probably be placed at a discount to market yields."
Foreign investors typically favour longer-dated issues, because they allow them to secure current high yields, which are expected to trend lower.
For the same reason, the series 24011 bonds are likely to attract foreign interest, as they are one of only two issues of OFZ interest-bearing bonds paying a semi-annual rather than quarterly coupon.
Interest is set on a coupon when the previous coupon is paid and can fall sharply from one coupon to the next.
Prices rose across the board on Tuesday. Shorter-dated issues rose as some operators took profits in long maturities and switched funds into shorter dates, dealers said.
But other operators were buying longer-dated paper in the hope of strong price rises on Thursday from investors who fail to get all their bids at Wednesday's auctions.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
